notes: Event date: 1-2 April 1945, one minute before midnight (Stacey, p. 545). Event definition: Army headquarters takes control of the 2nd Canadian Corps operations east of the Rhine at one minute before midnight of 1-2 April; at noon on 2 April the 1st British Corps returns to the command of General Dempsey after serving under General Crerar since Normandy, and the 1st Canadian Corps is now under the Army in the Arnhem sector. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 545: "At one minute before midnight of 1-2 April Headquarters First Canadian Army took control of the 2nd Canadian Corps' operations east of the Rhine"; "Crocker's 1st British Corps had returned to General Dempsey's command"; "General Foulkes' 1st Canadian Corps now under the Army in the Arnhem sector". Location: Nijmegen area, Gelderland (existing place PL0554) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Nijmegen, standing for the Army area; it is not a headquarters position. Location support: Stacey names no headquarters place for 2 April; the Army sector then ran from the Nijmegen salient to the Arnhem sector (p. 545). Commander: Gen. H. D. G. Crerar (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 663: 20 Mar. 44 to 30 Jul. 45).

current_activity: Montgomery visits Crerar's headquarters at Grave and outlines the advance to the Elbe
notes: Event date: 12 April 1945 (Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 571: "On the 12th the Corps Commander had issued instructions"; p. 572: "on the same day on which General Foulkes issued these instructions ... Field-Marshal Montgomery came to General Crerar's headquarters at Grave"). Event definition: the army headquarters is at Grave. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Location: Grave, Noord-Brabant (place PL0824), town centre, precision 5 km. Location support: Stacey names the headquarters at Grave. composing_text: CAN-COR-001C (1st Canadian Corps, visited by the Army Commander at Apeldoorn)
current_activity: Crerar learns of the surrender talks at 12:55, flies to Apeldoorn; the Army ceases fire at 08:00 on 5 May
notes: Event date: 4 May 1945 (Stacey, pp. 609-611). Event definition: Brigadier Belchem telephones General Crerar at 12:55 about the negotiations with the Germans; in the afternoon the Army Commander flies to Apeldoorn to explain the developments to General Foulkes, and the order issued that evening stops all offensive operations of the Army with all fire to cease from 08:00 on 5 May. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 609: "At 12:55 p.m. on 4 May Brigadier Belchem of Field-Marshal Montgomery"; p. 610: "when the Army Commander flew to"; "Apeldoorn in the afternoon"; p. 611: "cease forthwith and that all fire will cease from 0800 hrs tomorrow Saturday 5 May has been issued". Location: Apeldoorn, Gelderland with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the place of the visit of the Army Commander that afternoon, not a headquarters position; the Army headquarters place is not stated. Location support: Stacey says the Army Commander flew to Apeldoorn in the afternoon (p. 610), to explain the developments to General Foulkes of the 1st Corps; it does not say where the Army headquarters stood. Commander: Gen. H. D. G. Crerar (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 663: 20 Mar. 44 to 30 Jul. 45).
